Summarize Brown Heart Assistant..answer: The Brown Heart Assistant (BHAI) is a full‑stack, citation‑grounded health‑education platform that Pranav built and deployed from scratch for the Joshi Health Foundation, now serving more than 5,000 users alongside a searchable FAQ site[1].  It uses a router‑orchestrated multi‑agent architecture that integrates FAQ, MASALA Study, Instagram, YouTube and movie‑timestamp agents, each driven by source‑grounded prompts, confidence gating and medical‑safety refusal filters to ensure safe, accurate answers[1].  Under the hood, Pranav implemented hybrid retrieval that combines BM25, Azure PostgreSQL/pgvector, HNSWlib and NVIDIA embeddings with reciprocal‑rank‑fusion, and added a human‑in‑the‑loop tool that triggers on low‑confidence medical queries for doctor‑specialty matching or appointment booking[2].  The production backend includes Azure Blob artifact hydration, checksum validation, signed sessions, admin health checks, environment‑based model configuration, LangSmith tracing of agent runs and retrieval scores, and a suite of 113 passing tests, reflecting a self‑correcting RAG architecture that emphasizes reliability through query analysis, multi‑step evidence audits and confidence gating[3][2].

citations.title: RAG Reliability & Audits
citations.snippet: Pranav approaches RAG reliability by building self-correcting architectures. In projects like Agentic Graph-RAG (The Brain) and Brown Heart Assistant, he ensures high reliability using query analysis, hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector matching), Neo4j knowledge graphs, multi-step evidence sufficiency audits, confidence gating thresholds, and medical-safety refusal filters to prevent hallucinations.

How does he approach RAG reliability?.answer: Pranav tackles RAG reliability by designing self‑correcting architectures that continuously audit and refine the retrieval process. He begins with thorough query analysis and employs hybrid retrieval that combines BM25 keyword search with dense vector matching (FAISS/Pinecone) alongside a large Neo4j knowledge graph to surface relevant evidence [1]. His systems then run multi‑step evidence‑sufficiency audits, apply confidence‑gating thresholds and medical‑safety refusal filters to block hallucinations, and, when needed, expand searches to the web or Wikipedia via Tavily and use HyDE query expansion to improve failed queries [2]. These layered checks and refinements ensure higher hit rates and greater faithfulness in the final answers.

citations.title: Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain
citations.snippet: Pranav built 'Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain', a self-correcting LangGraph agent that audits evidence sufficiency, expands searches to web/Wikipedia via Tavily when needed, verifies supporting snippets, and refines failed queries with HyDE query expansion before answering. It uses hybrid retrieval across FAISS/Pinecone dense vectors, BM25, and a 311K-node / 374K-edge Neo4j knowledge graph over 39K chunks, unified with NVIDIA and Cross-Encoder reranking. On 100 judged SQuAD-style examples it improved retrieval hit rate from 82% to 92% and LLM-judged faithfulness from 0.708 to 0.847.
